steps.prompt: Are there signs of a serious allergic reaction? (Difficulty breathing, throat swelling, widespread rash, dizziness, collapse.)
This may be anaphylaxis. Call emergency services immediately. If the person has an epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen), use it now. Lay them down with legs raised unless breathing is difficult.
steps.cta: Use EpiPen if available and call emergency services

steps.prompt: If a bee stinger is still in the skin, scrape it out sideways with a fingernail or the edge of a card. Do not squeeze or use tweezers — this injects more venom.
Wash the area with soap and water. Apply a cold pack or wrapped ice for 10 minutes to reduce swelling and pain.
Calamine lotion, antihistamine cream, or oral antihistamine can relieve itching and local swelling. Keep the bite area clean and do not scratch.
